paragraphs.title: Quiet Reliance on God in the Face of Enemies

easy.explanation: The psalmist says, “Truly my soul waiteth upon God.”
easy.q: Upon whom does the psalmist’s soul wait silently?

easy.explanation: God is called the psalmist’s rock, salvation, and defence.
easy.q: What is God to the psalmist?

answers: They imagine mischief and seek to cast him down
easy.explanation: They plot against him and seek to cast him down.
easy.q: What do the enemies do against the man?

medium.explanation: God is his rock, salvation, and defence.
medium.q: Why will the psalmist not be greatly moved?

answers: A place of protection and strength
medium.explanation: God is presented as the psalmist’s protection and strong refuge.
medium.q: What does “defence” mean in this passage?

answers: They are silent outwardly and inwardly
They bless with their mouth but curse inwardly
They curse with their mouth but bless inwardly
medium.explanation: Their outward words differ from their inward hatred.
medium.q: What contrast appears in the enemies’ speech and intentions?

answers: He is vulnerable and near collapse
He is protected from every danger
challenge.explanation: Both images describe something unstable and easily brought down.
challenge.q: What do the bowing wall and tottering fence suggest about the man’s situation?

answers: It shows trust in God rather than reliance on retaliation
It proves the psalmist agrees with the enemies
It shows confidence in the enemies’ strength
challenge.explanation: The psalmist waits for God’s salvation despite the enemies’ attacks.
challenge.q: How is waiting silently related to the enemies’ threats?

answers: The psalmist is uncertain about trusting God
The enemies are his source of safety
God is the central source of security
challenge.explanation: The repetition highlights God as the only sure refuge.
challenge.q: What does the repeated description of God as rock and salvation emphasize?

paragraphs.title: God as the Source of Hope, Honor, and Refuge

easy.explanation: He says, “my expectation is from him.”
easy.q: From whom does the psalmist’s expectation come?

easy.explanation: The psalm says, “In God is my salvation and my glory.”
easy.q: What does God provide for the psalmist?

easy.explanation: He calls to “ye people” to trust in God.
easy.q: Whom does the psalmist call to trust in God?

medium.explanation: The verse says, “pour out your heart before him.”
medium.q: What are the people told to do before God?

answers: To openly bring one’s troubles and feelings to God
medium.explanation: The expression describes open and honest prayer before God.
medium.q: What does “pour out your heart before him” mean in context?

answers: He is their refuge and source of strength
He removes all people from the earth
medium.explanation: God is called a refuge, rock, salvation, and strength.
medium.q: Why should the people trust in God?

answers: Continued confidence and patient dependence on God
challenge.explanation: The repetition reinforces patient trust in God.
challenge.q: What does the repeated call to wait upon God emphasize?

answers: Trust in God is presented as a shared calling
The people are the source of salvation
The psalmist does not believe in God
challenge.explanation: His personal confidence becomes an invitation to the whole community.
challenge.q: Why does the psalmist address the people, not only himself?

answers: They are all presented as gifts or provisions of God
They are all weaknesses of mankind
They are all connected with robbery
challenge.explanation: The passage identifies God as the source of each of these blessings.
challenge.q: How are salvation, glory, strength, and refuge connected?

paragraphs.title: The Emptiness of Human Power and Wealth

easy.explanation: The passage calls them “vanity” and “a lie.”
easy.q: How are men of low and high degree described?

easy.explanation: It says, “Trust not in oppression, and become not vain in robbery.”
easy.q: What does the psalm warn people not to trust in?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “if riches increase, set not your heart upon them.”
easy.q: What should a person not do when riches increase?

medium.explanation: They are lighter than vanity when weighed in the balance.
medium.q: Why should people not place their confidence in human beings?

medium.explanation: The verse warns against setting one’s heart on increasing wealth.
medium.q: What does “riches” mean in this passage?

answers: They are unreliable objects of trust
medium.explanation: The passage warns that neither injustice nor wealth can provide lasting security.
medium.q: What do oppression, robbery, and riches have in common in this passage?

challenge.explanation: They are described as lighter than vanity in the balance.
challenge.q: What does the balance image convey about human beings?

answers: Increase does not make wealth a permanent foundation
challenge.explanation: The warning rejects wealth as the center of a person’s trust.
challenge.q: Why should increased riches not receive the heart?

answers: The preceding passage presents God as refuge, while this one rejects trust in human and material things
Both passages present wealth as the source of hope
The preceding passage concerns robbery, while this one presents God as refuge
challenge.explanation: The earlier verses direct trust toward God; these verses warn against relying on people or wealth.
challenge.q: What contrast exists between this passage and the preceding one?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “power belongeth unto God.”
The psalm says, “unto thee, O Lord, belongeth mercy.”
easy.q: What belongs to the Lord alongside power?

easy.explanation: God renders to every man according to his work.
easy.q: How does God repay every man?

answers: His power is joined with mercy
medium.explanation: The verses identify both God’s power and His mercy.
medium.q: What does the combination of power and mercy reveal about God?

medium.explanation: The phrase connects God’s repayment with each person’s actions.
medium.q: What does “according to his work” mean?

answers: People are repaid according to their deeds
People are not responsible for their actions
People are judged only by their wealth
medium.explanation: The verse presents a direct connection between conduct and repayment.
medium.q: How does this passage relate to human responsibility?

answers: God’s power is joined with mercy and righteous judgment
challenge.explanation: The passage combines divine strength, mercy, and just repayment.
challenge.q: What balance of ideas appears in the final verses?

answers: A person is evaluated by his conduct
challenge.explanation: The statement emphasizes the moral significance of human behavior.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from God’s repayment of every person according to his work?

answers: They direct confidence back to God and emphasize human accountability
They call people to trust in robbery and wealth
They claim that man is stronger than God
challenge.explanation: The psalm ends by affirming God’s power and mercy and the importance of each person’s works.
challenge.q: How do these verses summarize the psalm’s message?
